title: Oncall ops bulletin - week of 2026-05-22
body:
Purpose:
This weekly bulletin summarizes on-call activity, active incidents, SLO health, recent handoffs, runbook edits, and action items for the SRE team covering 2026-05-22 to 2026-05-28. Intended audience: SREs, infra eng, platform, and product owners who own SLAs/SLOs.

TL;DR:
- Three noteworthy incidents this week; none required customer-facing outage notices but two had measurable SLO impact.
- Overall error budget burn this week: 18% of monthly budget consumed (accelerated due to incident B).
- Immediate action items: stabilize auth cache (owner Aisha), short-term throttling rule for embeddings (owner Marco), update runbook for KV cache recovery (owner Evan).

1) Incident summaries (concise)

Incident A: Auth token storm — 2026-05-23 03:10 UTC
- Scope/impact: Increased 5xx rates from hosted-api control-plane for ~28 minutes, elevated API error rate to customers with small percentage of requests returning 503. P50 latency unaffected, p95 increased slightly.
- Root cause hypothesis: Burst of token refresh requests bypassed local auth-cache due to cache eviction race on scale-up.
- Mitigation taken: Rolled back a recent autoscaler config change to reduce concurrent init paths, applied a short TTL increase for auth-cache, enabled emergency throttling of refresh endpoints for anonymous clients.
- Follow-ups (short): JIRA-4821 created to add stronger cache priming logic and observability for cache misses. Owner: Aisha Khan.
- Long-term: Rework token refresh flow to avoid synchronous remote calls during cold-start; target in Q3.

Incident B: Embeddings batching regression — 2026-05-25 14:05 UTC
- Scope/impact: Sustained token latency increases and memory pressure on dedicated embedding workers; some requests time out at >30s. Affected Dedicated customers on region eu-west-1 using embedding-heavy pipelines.
- Root cause: A recent change in batch boundary heuristics (runtime PR #1297) increased max-batch size under certain request-size distributions, causing OOMs and GC spikes.
- Mitigation: Reverted the heuristic in prod, scaled embedding pool by +20% while patches are tested. Applied temporary circuit breaker to reject oversized batches instead of retrying.
- Follow-ups: JIRA-4833 for patch and test harness; add load-testing scenario for embeddings skew. Owner: Marco Alvarez.
- Customer comms: CS notified two affected customers; no SLA credits issued after verification but monitoring continues.

Incident C: KV cache sync lag during maintenance window — 2026-05-27 01:40 UTC
- Scope/impact: Intermittent increases in generation tail latency (p99) for a subset of private deployments on-prem where KV replication lagged during rolling kernel updates.
- Root cause: Replication backoff logic interacted poorly with transient network flaps during host reboots.
- Mitigation: Forced KV re-sync and extended the maintenance-window backoff to 5 minutes to allow nodes to fully rejoin before leader elections.
- Follow-ups: Update on-prem install docs and add explicit pre-checks in the roll script. Owner: Evan Park.

2) SLO & health snapshot
- Observability notes: New trace attribute "kv_replica_lag_ms" added to span set; dashboard widget created on confluence:ops/slo-health-dashboard.
- Key metrics (monthly SLOs, percent of successful requests):
  - Hosted API availability SLO (target 99.95% monthly): current month 99.86% (error budget remaining 0.09% -> ~18% burned this week).
  - Dedicated throughput SLO (p95 tail latency < 450ms for small payloads): currently 92% success for the month.
  - Embeddings worker memory SLO (OOM-free operation): 98.9% this month (incident B contributed to drop).
- Action: Temporary restriction placed on batch concurrency for embeddings until patched.

3) On-call handoffs and schedule notes
- Handoff summary for 2026-05-28 morning shift:
  - Outgoing: Aisha Khan (night shift) — left notes about auth-cache traces and the A-ticket status.
  - Incoming: Marco Alvarez — please pick up JIRA-4833 and verify embedding pool autoscale dashboards (dash: infra/embedding-pool).
- Mid-week swap: Evan Park will swap dates with Priya Desai on 2026-06-02 due to travel. Calendar updated.
- Paging & escalation changes: Reminder to use escalation path v2 (Slack #sre-escalate -> PagerDuty) for incidents with >5 minutes escalation target. New escalation doc: confluence:ops/escalation-v2.

4) Runbooks & playbook edits (completed this week)
- Auth-cache runbook: added cache-miss troubleshooting steps and quick TTL bump play (author: Aisha).
- KV cache recovery: added forced re-sync commands and leader election diagnostic steps (author: Evan).
- Embeddings rollback playbook: added a rollback checklist and temporary throttling knobs (author: Marco).
- Note: please review runbooks before next on-call rotation; runbook links appended to the weekly SRE index.

5) Action items (owners + due dates)
- Aisha Khan: Implement cache priming on scale-up (JIRA-4821) — due 2026-06-10.
- Marco Alvarez: Complete embedding heuristic patch + unit + load tests (JIRA-4833) — due 2026-06-03.
- Evan Park: Add pre-checks and clearer rollback steps to on-prem roll script — due 2026-06-05.
- Priya Desai (me): Coordinate a post-incident deep-dive meeting for incident B (invite Q2 contributors and product owners) — proposed 2026-06-01.

6) Notes on capacity and upcoming windows
- Capacity: embedding pool utilization peaked at 78% this week; recommend temporary +15% buffer for EU regions during heavy ML retraining (teams notified).
- Change freeze reminder: There is a soft change freeze on 2026-06-20 for the customer-facing demo week; any infra-impacting changes need approval.

7) Retrospective highlights & takeaways
- Observability gaps: missing explicit batching metrics and per-batch memory footprints made root cause analysis slower than we'd like. Action: add batch-size and per-batch memory metric to the runtime exporter.
- Defensive defaults: under load, prefer conservative batch-size heuristics with fast-fail circuit breakers to avoid cascading OOMs.
- Communication: nightly on-call notes were helpful; continue the short-form note style used here.

Appendix: quick links and contact points
- On-call rota: gdrive:team/sre/oncall-2026 (calendar invite attached)
- Incident runbooks: confluence:ops/runbooks (auth-cache, kv-cache, embeddings)
- Slack channels: #sre, #sre-escalate, #platform-notices

If anything missing or if you'd like a deeper RCA for any incident, ping me (Priya) or add to linked_artifacts.

-- End bulletin --
